title: Securities & Financial Glossary
subtitle: 40+ plain-language definitions for retail investors in India
summary: Quick reference encyclopedia explaining financial jargon, bond metrics, tax terms, and depository concepts in simple words.
disclaimer: Educational information only. Not investment advice. TradeOne is not a SEBI-registered investment adviser. Rules, taxes and yields change; verify with official sources.

terms.definition: Interest earned on a bond since the last coupon payment date, which the buyer pays the seller upon purchase.
Annual Information Statement - an Income Tax Department portal view showing all interest, dividends, and securities sales linked to your PAN.
Application Supported by Blocked Amount - an investor's bank account holds the bid money until securities allotment occurs.
Distributing investments among various asset classes like equities, debt, real estate, and cash according to risk capacity.
A unique 16-digit number assigned to every demat account holder by NSDL or CDSL.
One-hundredth of a percentage point (0.01%). For example, 50 bps equals 0.50%.
The price of a bond excluding accrued interest.
The total invoice price of a bond, including both the clean price and accrued interest.
A government contract granting an infrastructure operator the right to build, operate, and collect toll revenue for a specified number of years.
An event initiated by a public company affecting shareholders, such as dividends, stock splits, bonuses, or rights issues.
The fixed annual interest percentage paid by a bond issuer on its face value.
An assessment by independent rating agencies (e.g. CRISIL, ICRA) measuring the creditworthiness of a borrower.
The probability that a borrower or bond issuer will fail to pay interest or repay principal on schedule.
The lowest successful price accepted by the RBI in an auction, which sets the yield for allotted non-competitive bidders.
A SEBI-registered entity legally bound to protect the collective interests of corporate debenture holders and monitor collateral.
The risk that a bond issuer defaults completely on its debt obligations.
A dematerialized electronic account holding shares, bonds, mutual funds, and trust units securely under NSDL or CDSL.
An intermediary (like a bank or stockbroker) registered with NSDL or CDSL that manages retail demat accounts.
A risk management strategy that mixes a wide variety of uncorrelated investments within a portfolio.
A financial ratio showing how much a company pays out in dividends each year relative to its current share price.
The nominal par value stated by the issuer, usually ₹100 for G-Secs or ₹1,000/₹10,000 for corporate debentures, on which coupon interest is calculated.
Investments that pay a return on a fixed periodic schedule with fixed or predictable cash flows.
Government Security - a tradable debt instrument issued by the Central or State Governments of India.
The danger that the purchasing power of cash flows from an investment will erode due to rising consumer prices.
The risk that rising market interest rates will cause the market price of existing fixed-rate bonds to fall.
Infrastructure Investment Trust - a pooled investment trust owning operational infrastructure assets like highways and power grids.
International Securities Identification Number - a 12-character alphanumeric code uniquely identifying a specific security globally.
The ease and speed with which an asset can be converted into cash without causing significant price impact.
Long-Term Capital Gain - profits from selling assets held beyond the specified long-term holding period (over 12 months for listed securities).
The calendar date on which a bond's principal amount becomes due and is repaid to the investor.
A measure of a bond's price sensitivity to interest rate movements, estimating percentage price change for a 1% shift in yield.
Net Distributable Cash Flows - the cash remaining after operational costs and debt servicing that REITs and InvITs must distribute to unitholders.
A corporate bond that cannot be converted into equity shares, offering fixed coupon returns.
Online Bond Platform Provider - a SEBI-registered digital platform facilitating retail investment in listed debt securities.
The face value of a bond (100% of face value). Trading 'above par' means at a premium; 'below par' means at a discount.
A free online portal operated by the Reserve Bank of India allowing individual retail investors to directly buy Government Securities and T-Bills.
Real Estate Investment Trust - a trust that owns and manages commercial income-generating real estate properties.
Sovereign Gold Bond - government-backed securities denominated in grams of gold, paying 2.50% annual interest with tax-free redemption at maturity.
An explicit guarantee backed by the Government of India, representing the highest credit safety in Indian Rupees.
Special Purpose Vehicle - a subsidiary company established by a REIT or InvIT to hold underlying assets or project rights.
Short-Term Capital Gain - profits from selling assets held for 12 months or less.
Treasury Bill - a short-term zero-coupon sovereign debt paper issued by the Government of India with 91, 182, or 364 day tenors.
Tax Deducted at Source - tax deducted upfront by an payer and credited to the government on behalf of the payee.
An investor who owns units of a mutual fund, REIT, or InvIT, entitled to proportional distributions and voting rights.
Weighted Average Lease Expiry - a metric measuring the average remaining lease duration across all corporate tenants in a REIT's property portfolio.
The total annualized return an investor anticipates earning if a bond is purchased at current market price and held until maturity.
